answer: A remote hardware attestation protocol curbs Sybil attacks in an agent economy monitoring pearl reefs. Each node relies on a silicon trust anchor to measure memory state and execute an attested cryptographic kernel during peer handshakes. An attacker incurs the verifiable cost of provisioning dedicated secure microcontrollers per identity rather than spinning up virtual containers. However, physical side-channel leakage from memory buses can compromise signing keys, undermining verification.
